sub_unit_name: Potable water and its specifications - Steps involved in the treatment of potable water -Disinfection of potable water by chlorination and break - point chlorination

content.title: What is Potable Water?
content.description: Potable water is water that is safe for drinking and domestic use. It is free from harmful microorganisms, toxic chemicals, objectionable taste, odor, and suspended impurities.

content.content: Potable water should be clear, colorless, odorless, and safe for human consumption. It must satisfy physical, chemical, and biological quality standards prescribed by drinking water authorities.

content.title: Importance of Potable Water
content.content: Safe drinking water prevents water-borne diseases such as cholera, typhoid, dysentery, and hepatitis, ensuring good public health.
Natural water contains suspended particles, dissolved salts, microorganisms, and organic matter. Water treatment removes these impurities to make water suitable for drinking.

items.question: Screening
items.answer: Removes large floating materials such as leaves, sticks, and debris.

items.question: Aeration
items.answer: Removes dissolved gases and improves the taste and odor of water.

items.question: Coagulation and Sedimentation
items.answer: Alum is added to form flocs that settle down with suspended impurities.

items.question: Filtration
items.answer: Sand filters remove fine suspended particles and microorganisms.

items.question: Disinfection
items.answer: Kills disease-causing microorganisms before water is supplied.

content.content: Chlorination is the most widely used method of disinfecting potable water. Chlorine destroys harmful bacteria, viruses, and other pathogens while leaving a small residual amount that protects water during distribution.

content.title: Principle of Chlorination
content.description: When chlorine is added to water, it forms hypochlorous acid (HOCl), a powerful disinfecting agent that destroys microorganisms.

content.content:
Cl₂ + H₂O → HOCl + HCl
HOCl ⇌ H⁺ + OCl⁻
Hypochlorous acid (HOCl) is the main disinfecting species responsible for killing microorganisms.

Break-point chlorination is the process of adding chlorine until all organic matter, ammonia, and reducing substances are oxidized. Beyond this point, free residual chlorine remains in water, ensuring effective disinfection.

items.question: Low Cost
items.answer: Economical and suitable for large-scale water treatment.

items.question: Residual Protection
items.answer: Prevents microbial contamination during storage and distribution.

items.question: Easy Operation
items.answer: Simple to apply and monitor in water treatment plants.

content.title: Residual Chlorine
content.content: A residual chlorine concentration of about 0.2–0.5 mg/L is generally maintained to ensure continued protection against microbial contamination.

content.title: Quick Revision
points: Potable water is safe for drinking and domestic use.
Water treatment includes screening, aeration, coagulation, sedimentation, filtration, and disinfection.
Chlorination is the most common method of water disinfection.
Hypochlorous acid (HOCl) is the active disinfecting agent.
Break-point chlorination ensures complete oxidation and leaves free residual chlorine.
